newsitem.title: USA: US WCoast prods drift sideways, most signs bearish.
newsitem.headline: US WCoast prods drift sideways, most signs bearish.

text.p: U.S. West Coast product prices drifted sideways late Friday, with activity thin and most signals bearish except inventories.
"Inventories are the big joker in the pack. It there's a refinery problem prices will take off," one broker said.
An unexpected plant shutdown could cut supplies already diminished by lower-than-normal output and planned refinery maintenance, traders said.
West Coast gasoline stocks fell 709,000 barrels last week to 26.9 million barrels -- an extremely low volume, they said.
Total refinery output remained below normal at 89.6 percent of capacity, versus typical levels in the low to mid-90s.

Technicals offset bullish stocks, with NYMEX October gasoline adding a 0.23 cent loss to Thursday's slide of 1.74 cent a gallon. The contract settled 61.09 cents a gallon Friday, weighed by high imports and waning demand.

Conventional or "clear" grade gasoline in Los Angeles remained 64/65 cents a gallon. Discounts for San Francisco grade were two cents under. Premium conventional in L.A. was 10 cents over regular on ongoing problems with key Mobil gasoline unit, and new rumors of a possible reformer problem at a Texaco plant.
CARB gasoline in L.A. held at 68.50/69 cents a gallon.
Bids for CARB diesel in L.A. were unchanged at 73.50/75 cents and low sulphur flattened at 68.50/69.50 cents.
